trigger: Procurement security questionnaire before panel appointment

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: Daniel, thanks for joining. I have you as Daniel Ortiz, operations lead at Kite & Co, a commercial law firm in the CBD. What prompted the conversation with Harbourline IT?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Daniel Ortiz
turns.text: That's right. We're reviewing our panel of suppliers after a procurement refresh. IT support is bundled into that, partly because our partners have started asking for clearer security reporting.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: What does the partner group want to see that they aren't getting today?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Daniel Ortiz
turns.text: They want fewer surprises. When a barrister can't access a brief or a senior associate is locked out before court, it becomes an operational incident. The current provider fixes things eventually, but there's no rhythm or account management.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: How are your systems set up across document management, Microsoft 365 and remote access?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Daniel Ortiz
turns.text: We're on Microsoft 365, Xero for finance, and a cloud document platform for matters. Remote access is mostly browser based, but some partners still have old habits around local files and personal devices.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: Who will decide whether a new provider is worth moving to?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Daniel Ortiz
turns.text: The managing partner signs off, the finance director checks the numbers, and procurement controls the process. I can recommend a shortlist, but I can't award it on this call.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: What would make you confident enough to recommend Harbourline IT for that shortlist?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Daniel Ortiz
turns.text: I need evidence that you understand confidentiality, response times and change management. We're ninety-five staff, but partner influence makes us feel larger. A botched migration would be painful politically.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: Where are the current risks most visible day to day?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Daniel Ortiz
turns.text: Joiners and leavers are messy, shared mailboxes are inconsistent, and procurement keeps asking me for supplier documents I have to chase. There's also a cyber insurance renewal in November, but it's not the only driver.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: At that size, the managed services agreement would normally sit around $140 per seat per month, with a scoped onboarding project for identity, device management and documentation.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Daniel Ortiz
turns.text: Procurement will not let us progress without the full questionnaire and insurance certificates. They will ask about data handling, subcontractors, incident response and professional indemnity before a partner even reads the proposal.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: That makes sense. I can answer the supplier side and show our standard controls, although some items depend on the final scope. I will send the security pack and a sample service schedule so you can test whether procurement is comfortable.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Daniel Ortiz
turns.text: That would help, but it may disappear into the vendor portal for a while. Our procurement manager is methodical and the managing partner is away until the week after next.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: Would it be useful to pencil a review with the managing partner when he is back?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Daniel Ortiz
turns.text: Possibly, but I don't want to put a date in before procurement accepts the documents. If they bounce the questionnaire, the partner call would be premature.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: Understood. I will send the pack and service schedule today, and you can tell me what procurement comes back with.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Daniel Ortiz
turns.text: Yes, send it through. I'm interested, but I need the process to move first. Once procurement clears the basics, we can talk about who joins the next call.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: The sample service schedule will spell out response targets, account review cadence and what evidence is produced monthly. That way procurement can compare more than hourly rates.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Daniel Ortiz
turns.text: That will be useful. They tend to reduce vendors to a spreadsheet, and IT support is hard to compare unless the service boundaries are explicit.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: If procurement wants clarification, I can answer in writing or join a short call with them before the partner group spends time on it.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Daniel Ortiz
turns.text: Possibly. I need to see how they react first. They can be quite strict about keeping suppliers out until the formal shortlist is set.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: No problem. I will make the pack self-contained, including our insurance certificates, data handling summary and a plain-English incident response outline.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Daniel Ortiz
turns.text: That gives me a decent chance of getting it through the first gate. After that the internal politics are the bigger unknown.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: I will also avoid assuming the current provider has done nothing. The comparison should be about service evidence and accountability, not throwing stones at people who may have been operating under a loose brief.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Daniel Ortiz
turns.text: That tone will help. The partners dislike vendor drama, and the incumbent still supports us while this process runs.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: Thanks Daniel. I will keep it concise and label the parts procurement usually wants first.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Daniel Ortiz
turns.text: Appreciated. That will make my life easier even if the timetable isn't completely in my hands.
